_about: SC (Twin Dial round 3): tab 2's page - the check-control message in the centre window, the other listed messages as rows, the empty and pointer states, the warning tab's looks. Panel px (1920 x 720). Read by tools/twin-dial/r3/sc/centre_cc.js (the model) and card_draw.py (the preview / K2). Everything here is a DESIGN proposal for the lead (docs/twin-dial/r3/SC-REPORT.md); the page grammar (title, rule) is today's SPEC 6.2 until SF publishes its own. [B3: ported into the build; the counter's baseline is the SPEC-R3's 326, the rest is SC's.]

grammar._why: SF's measured grammar (bake/work/twin-dial/r3/pub/SF/pages.json, rev 1): title baseline ~281 (ours matches to 1 px), title rule y 295-297.5 (P: 2.5 px, code ~205), body below it; window [729, 172, 1191, 613]

title.widget: c_title (an existing text widget, conn 1; NOT part of the message's paint)

rule.colour: SF's proposal (code ~205); tdback rules[0]; option: the severity colour while tab 2 shows a card (see severity.where)

sheet._why: ONE image widget paints tab 2's whole body (card block, rows, counter, scroll indicator) in ONE paint, so 'our text for message K is on the screen' is one event per sheet send, exactly as round 2's plate. Its rect is the window's width (the scroll indicator sits at x 1189, SF) under the title rule.
sheet.conn_option_b: the one page sheet of all centre pages (see cost)
sheet.z: above every other centre layer (nothing of ours may overlap it while it shows a message)

card._what: the message the car says it shows NOW (TwinCC.candidate): the first block of the page, centred (VF's M1 'centre card' grammar: the symbol above, the words below), so a line gets the window's whole width
card.cell_fill: by severity (severity.colours.cell); grey: the tab ramp 0.002 -> 0.16 linear, top to bottom (as round 2's plate)

symbol.name: shared/twin_cc.js symbolFor(id, colour) (VT's table, generic by colour)

headline.cut: words wrapped greedily; what does not fit in three lines ends line 3 with the ellipsis (round 2's rule, one line more)
headline.capacity_note: Noto 42 lower-case Cyrillic averages 25.5 px (td_msg advances): about 17 letters per line, about 50 in three lines. The names seen on the car so far are 14, 16, 27 and 37 characters long (MC-REPORT). The left-aligned variant (cell left, text from x 833) gives only 13 letters per line: rejected, kept for the mockups as 'card_left'

counter.when: the car gives a frame n of m (statusMenuCCMessage) and that frame is this message (round 2's TwinCC._counter); top right of the sheet, beside the cell, clear of the headline
counter._build: B3 (Twin Dial 0.1.1): baseline 326 as SPEC-R3 5.1 says (SC proposed 334); SPEC-R3 wins

card.block_bottom: last baseline + 12 + 8 (444 / 491 / 538 for 1 / 2 / 3 lines); rows start 6 px lower
card.rows_after: 1 line: two rows; 2 lines: one row; 3 lines: none (the scroll indicator says more exist; the list page shows them once nothing shows now)

rows._what: every other ccList entry outside ignoreIds (the car's list holds active AND stored messages and cannot tell them apart: MC-REPORT A5). The card is the one shown now; a row is 'in the car's list'. Grammar: SF's list proposal for our window (pages.json list_page.proposal_P_for_our_window), without a selection bar (we have no key to move one; SB may add it).
rows.order: severity first (red, amber, then grey / white / green / default), then the car's own array order (stable). ccListRiskClass (RK10..RK900, unseen, probe P2) may replace the colour as the sort key once the probe shows it
rows.first_top: body_top (300) on the list page; card block bottom + 6 under a card

symbol.colour: by severity: red (218, 16, 48), amber (240, 170, 10), green (59, 155, 26), white otherwise; no cell

name.cut: one line; a longer name ends in the ellipsis

rows.separator: none (SF: the maker's list rows have none; the normal view has no borders)

scroll_indicator.thumb_len: visible / total of the track; at the top (we never scroll: no key yet)

rows.counts_as_our_text: a row counts as our text for its message only when its WHOLE name is drawn (not cut). A cut row never lets BMW's panel be covered.

pointer._what: tab 2 is selected, the car says a message shows, but ours cannot be drawn (D7, no entry, empty name, missing glyph, throw, sheet refused, release): a block that sends the driver to BMW's own panel. Our fixed words, never the message's: it never counts as our text for any message.
pointer.cell: as card.cell (centred), fill by the severity the machine knows (grey when none)
pointer.symbol: generic by colour: cc_warn (red / amber / unknown), cc_info (otherwise)

empty._what: tab 2 selected, no message shown, nothing listed

warning_tab._what: the tab's looks; the cell is [744, 812] of the bar, icon cc_warn 38 at (778, 143). 'Filled = selected' (the brief's reading of 02 / 06 / 08): the fill never carries severity in the recommended variant.

W0_nothing.when: no message shown, the list empty
W0_nothing.icon: white x 0.5 (dim, as the phone / navigation tabs' 'nothing there')

W2_message.when: a message shows (any state but none) and tab 2 is not selected
W2_message.icon: the severity colour: red (218, 16, 48), amber (240, 170, 10); white for grey / white / default / green

W3_selected.fill: the selection fill of every tab (SF; red on the references)

warning_tab.variant_S2: tab 2's selection fill takes the severity colour while a red or amber message shows (amber: black icon); the standard selection fill otherwise. Keeps round 2's look; mixes the two meanings of the fill (05 shows a green fill for its settings tab, so the references' fill colour does vary by tab)
warning_tab.variant_hidden: W0 hidden (the cell drawn without an icon): rejected - the bar's cells would change meaning by position

severity.from: ccList cCColor: RED red; YELLOW, ORANGE amber; GREEN green; WHITE, DEFAULT grey (SPEC 8.2, shared/twin_cc.js severityOf)
where: the warning tab's icon while tab 2 is NOT selected (W2)

the bottom rule y 611-615 while state is ours (round 2's tdback rules[1].ours, unchanged; 04 / 08 show the rule above the bottom row red while the warning tab is selected, 02 / 06 white with tab 1: hypothesis that the references colour it)
option: the title rule (tdback rules[0]) in the severity colour while tab 2 shows a card (needs an 'ours'-like entry keyed on tab 2: an additive contract change)
severity.night: as round 2's plate: shared/twin_cc.js nightRgb with SEVERITY[].mult / ruleMult; white text 0.80, grey 0.75

samples_for_mockups._why: invented, neutral Ukrainian, lengths like the car's (14-37 characters); never a real log's text
